clue.text: Deadlock contributing to mistrust and offence

indicators.note: the answer is a part that contributes to the run of letters in the next words, sitting inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Mutual suspicion and taking offence keep two parties stuck in a deadlock.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-off is a stalemate in which neither side will give way, which is what a deadlock is.

clue.text: Modify recusal not based on religion

indicators.note: to modify is to alter, so the letters of the next word are changed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A call to amend a judge's withdrawal from a case so it is not religiously motivated.
explanation.walkthrough: A recusal is when a judge steps aside from a case because of a conflict of interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Secular means worldly or civil, having no connection with religious matters.

clue.text: Work in a US city is torture

indicators.note: one word is placed in the others, enclosed by them

parts.note: taken as written
to go is to work or function, as a machine does
NY is the abbreviation for New York

explanation.surface: A complaint that working in an American city is sheer torture.
explanation.definitionFit: Agony is extreme physical or mental suffering, the kind torture inflicts.

clue.text: Criticize appeal with certain irritation

parts.note: dis is slang for to disrespect or criticise
a plea is an appeal
certain means sure

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a court appeal with obvious annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: Displeasure is a feeling of annoyance or dissatisfaction, much like irritation.

clue.text: Over a long period, scavenge

parts.note: for and over both mean during, as in 'for a week' or 'over a week'
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: An animal hunting for scraps over a long stretch of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to search around for food or provisions, which is how one scavenges.

clue.text: Trick of role reversal

indicators.note: the clue tells us outright that the word for a role is turned round

parts.note: an actor's role is a part

explanation.surface: A theatrical trick in which the actors swap roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversal' looks like part of the picture of actors swapping parts, but it is the instruction to read the word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is a trick or ruse designed to catch someone out, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: I arrive, wrecked, in popular seaside area

indicators.note: something wrecked is broken up, so the letters are smashed and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shipwrecked traveller washing up at a holiday coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riviera is the Mediterranean coastline of France and Italy, a famous holiday resort area.

clue.text: Is under average for capital

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means one part is written below the other

parts.note: par is a normal or average level
taken as written

explanation.surface: A city's financial capital is running below average.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests money; here it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris is the capital city of France, so it is one example of a capital.

clue.text: Get over being in a bad mood

explanation.surface: Advice to get over feeling grumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to traverse; as an adjective it means irritable or angry.

clue.text: Go through quickly and knock down on the way

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to review something briefly
second meaning: to hit with a vehicle on the road

explanation.surface: Someone rushing through a task and flattening something as they go.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to rehearse or review briskly and to strike someone with a car or other vehicle.

clue.text: Practical details in the form of witty rhymes

parts.words: in the form of witty rhymes
parts.note: surface reading: put into clever verse
setter's reading: the two halves of the answer each rhyme with witty

explanation.surface: Setting out the practical points as clever rhyming verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a rhyming pair, and both halves rhyme with 'witty', so the clue describes its shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the basic practical facts of a matter, the real details.

clue.text: Unlike Ministers prepare

definitions.meaning: first meaning: not of the clergy, as ministers of religion are
second meaning: to set out, as one does a table

explanation.surface: A political jibe that, unlike the government's Ministers, someone actually prepares.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital M makes Ministers look like government members; here they are ministers of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay people are those not ordained as clergy, and to lay a table or plan is to prepare it.

clue.text: Fair quality that makes things easy to convey

definitions.meaning: first meaning: paleness of colouring, as in fair hair or skin

definitions.text: that makes things easy to convey
definitions.meaning: second meaning: lack of weight, making something easy to carry

explanation.surface: Praise for a fair-minded quality that helps get ideas across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' suggests justice and 'convey' suggests communicating; they mean pale colour and physically carrying.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both paleness of shade and having little weight, which makes carrying easy.

clue.text: Type of music that's good with enthusiastic backing around

indicators.note: something backing goes in the reverse direction, so the word is read from its end
one part is placed around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: enthusiastic means eager
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A style of music that sounds good when it has keen backing singers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' fits the musical picture of a backing band, but it is the signal to turn a word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Reggae is a genre of popular music from Jamaica, so it is an example of a type of music.

clue.text: Good sense I displayed differently in first book

indicators.note: something displayed in a different way has its parts arranged in another order

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
taken as written

explanation.surface: Showing sound judgement presented in a new way in an opening volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis is the first book of the Bible, so it is the first book in that collection.

clue.text: How to cross range for major operation

parts.note: by means 'by means of', saying how something is done
a pass is a route through a mountain range

explanation.surface: Asking the best way across mountains for a big military operation.
explanation.walkthrough: Read together, the wordplay answers its own question: you cross a range by pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart bypass is a serious surgical procedure, so the answer names a major operation.

clue.text: Holy place can and must change

indicators.note: to change is to alter, so the letters before it are put in a new order

parts.note: the two words, with the joining word left out

explanation.surface: A declaration that a sacred place is able to, and has to, move with the times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the two words of fodder and gives no letters of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctum is a sacred or holy place, such as the inner part of a temple.

clue.text: Little time put into piece of Greek text, hence bad mark

indicators.note: one part is put into another, sitting inside it

parts.note: sigma is one character of the Greek alphabet
T is the short form for time

explanation.surface: A student spends too little time on a Greek translation and gets a poor grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad mark' sounds like a school grade; here it is a mark of disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of shame or discredit attached to someone, a figurative bad mark.

clue.text: Transport worker that helps cope with lightning strike

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the official who collects fares on a bus or train

definitions.text: that helps cope with lightning strike
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a metal rod that carries electricity safely to earth

explanation.surface: A transport worker who helps the public cope during a sudden walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action by transport staff; here it is a bolt of lightning hitting a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus conductor collects fares, and a lightning conductor is a rod that channels the charge to the ground.

clue.text: Clergyman authenticated collection of sacred works

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a priest on the staff of a cathedral
second meaning: the books accepted as genuine scripture

explanation.surface: A cleric who has verified a library of holy texts.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a cathedral cleric, and the biblical canon is the set of books recognised as genuine scripture.

clue.text: Is able to preserve French resort, we hear

parts.note: first meaning: has the ability
second meaning: to seal food in a tin

indicators.note: what we hear is the spoken sound, not the spelling

parts.note: Cannes, on the Riviera, sounds like this short word

explanation.surface: Someone is able to protect a French resort from development.
explanation.walkthrough: Three routes to one word: two meanings and a sound-alike of the film-festival town.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to be able to, and also to put food into tins to keep it.

clue.text: Firm belief of Conservative about party

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
re means about or concerning
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A Tory's firm conviction about their political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' suggests the political sort; it is a social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of beliefs or principles, from the Latin for 'I believe'.

clue.text: Receives inside information back — something to save for later

indicators.note: back tells us the combined letters are read in the opposite direction
one word goes inside another, which wraps round it

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
receives means gets

explanation.surface: Someone getting inside information back, worth keeping for future use.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is informal British for information, as in 'get the gen on something'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest egg is a sum of money put aside as savings for the future.

clue.text: Form of communication that's short, time after time

indicators.note: after says one part is placed following another in the line of letters

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
wee means small or short
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A form of messaging that's brief, sent over and over again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' is apt for the original 140-character limit, but it is just a synonym for small.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweet is a short message posted on the social media platform formerly called Twitter.

clue.text: One may run, producing narrow margin of victory

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a part of the face that runs when you have a cold
second meaning: a horse wins by this tiny distance

explanation.surface: A runner in a race who wins by the slimmest of leads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' suggests a race, which the second half supports; but it is the runny face part of a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A runny nose is common with a cold, and in horse racing to win by a nose is to win very narrowly.

clue.text: Very little loud noise when multiple deliveries happen

parts.note: baby as an adjective means very small
a boom is a deep loud sound

explanation.surface: A faint sound heard when many parcels arrive at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliveries' suggests post or parcels; it means births.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby boom is a period with a sharp rise in the birth rate, when many babies are delivered.
